notes: ⌘⇧V opens your history in the command palette, with the preview beside it and every action, Pause and Ignore Next Copy included, under ⌘K. The popup stays on the menu bar icon.
Every copy now has a preview, short ones too, so the palette's list keeps its detail pane and stops jumping as you move through it.
Search finds images by the text in them, read on your Mac with Apple's text recognition, and Copy Text in Image (⌘⇧T) copies it.
The menu bar icon is off by default: ⌘⇧V and the palette open the history. It comes back while recording is paused, and Settings can keep it on.
Agents can no longer read your clipboard unless you allow it in Stackbar's Settings → Agents.
Matching copies show in the command palette's own results as you type, so you can paste one without opening the history first (Stackbar 0.20.0). Turn it off in Settings.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.clipboard.description:
Everything you copy, searchable, pinnable and one keystroke from being pasted
back. ⌘⇧V opens it in the palette from anywhere, with a preview of the
selected copy beside the list: type to filter, ↑↓ and Return (or ⌘1 to ⌘9)
to paste into the app you were in, ⌥Return to paste as plain text, ⌘P to pin
and ⌥⌫ to delete. Formatted text keeps its formatting, and images are kept by
the host and pasted back. The text in a copied image (a screenshot, a
photo of a receipt) is read on your Mac, so typing finds the image, and ⌘⇧T
copies that text. ⌘K holds every action, Pause Recording and Ignore Next
Copy included. The popup with the last copy and the Pause buttons is still on
the menu bar icon, if you turn the icon on.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the clipboard. Passwords are skipped: the host never hands out items an app marks as concealed or transient, and copies from password managers (or any app you add) are ignored. Copies that look like secrets (API keys and tokens, JSON web tokens, private keys, card numbers, six-digit codes) are shown masked, kept out of agent tools, and dropped after 15 minutes unless you pin them.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, window, settings. Hotkey ⌘⇧V.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: how many items to keep, the order, pasting directly or only copying, showing matching copies in the palette's results, keeping images, finding images by their text, plain text by default, how long to keep secrets (not at all, 5 minutes to an hour, or like any copy), apps and text patterns to ignore, and pausing the history.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Clipboard History, Paste Last Copy as Plain Text, Pause Clipboard History, Ignore Next Copy.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `recent_clips`, `search_clips` and `copy_clip`.

facts.label: Requires
facts.text: Stackbar 0.27.0 or later.

notes: The menu bar icon is off by default, since the switcher lives on a held key. It comes back by itself when the key stops working, and Settings can keep it on.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
First release: hold Right ⌘ and press a letter to switch apps, and pin letters to the apps you use most.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.app-switche.description:
Switch apps without ⌘Tab. Hold **Right ⌘** and press an app's first letter:
S for Safari, X for Xcode. If several apps share a letter, pressing it again
moves to the next one. If only one does and it's already in front, pressing
it again hides it (or shows its next window, if you prefer). Letters with no
app pass through, so Right ⌘ C still copies.

To pin a letter, bring an app to the front and press **Right ⌘ ⌥** plus the
letter. A pinned letter opens the app even when it isn't running. Hold Right
⌘ on its own for a moment to see the whole letter map.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: `.keyLayer` and `.apps`. Stackbar listens to the keyboard and switches apps for the plugin, so Stackbar asks for Accessibility access the first time. Stackbar 0.16.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: the key you hold (Right ⌘, ⌥, ⌃ or ⇧), what pressing the letter of the app in front does, the letter map, automatic letters, and opening pinned apps.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Pin a Letter to an App, Clear App Switcher Pins.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `letters`.

facts.label: Not covered
facts.text: jumping between Spaces and a window grid. To find an app by name, type it in the palette (the Applications plugin); to snap windows, use Windows. While an app has Secure Input on, such as in a password field, macOS blocks every keyboard listener. The panel tells you which app has it on.

notes: Matches the way the rest of the palette does, with Stackbar's own matcher, so apps and commands rank on one scale. Stackbar now also learns which app you pick for what you type.
The panel points to App Switcher, for switching apps with Right ⌘ and a letter. It stays a separate plugin, because it listens to the keyboard.
Typing "settings" finds the System Settings app first. Every pane used to outrank it, because each one has "settings" as a keyword.
First release: the palette's app search, now a plugin.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.application.description:
Your apps and System Settings panes in the command palette, as Spotlight and
Raycast have them. Type a few letters ("saf", "vsc", "wi-fi") and the app
comes first in the results; Return opens it, ⌘K copies its path or bundle id.
The ones you open most rank higher. Search Applications lists them all.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the list of installed apps and opening them (`.apps`), and opening System Settings panes by their link. Stackbar 0.20.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel (your most opened apps).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Applications, which also feeds the palette's results.

facts.label: Looks in
facts.text: /Applications (one folder deep), ~/Applications and the system's own apps, plus every pane System Settings lists.

notes: First release.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.browser-tab.description:
Your open browser tabs and your bookmarks in the palette. Search Browser
Tabs lists every tab in Safari, Chrome, Arc, Brave and Edge while they run;
type part of a title or address and Return switches to it (⌘W closes it,
⌘⇧C copies the link). Search Bookmarks finds the bookmarks Chrome, Brave,
Edge and Vivaldi keep, and opens one in its browser.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: running `osascript` to read and switch tabs (macOS asks once to let Stackbar control each browser), `cat` to read each Chromium browser's `Bookmarks` file in its profile folder, and the list of running apps, so a browser that isn't open is never started. Stackbar 0.22.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel (the open tabs).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Browser Tabs, Search Bookmarks.

facts.label: Leaves out
facts.text: Safari's bookmarks, which macOS keeps behind Full Disk Access, and browser profiles other than the default one.

notes: The answer is always first in the palette, above a past answer to the same sum that the panel keeps.
The palette only asks Calculator about text that can have an answer.
A setting to turn currency conversion off. Off, no exchange rates are fetched and the plugin never goes online.
Currency conversion: `100 usd in eur`, `$50 to gbp`.
Times across zones: `5pm london in tokyo`, `now in sf`.
Asks for network access to fetch exchange rates.
First release: the palette's calculator, now a plugin.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.calculator.description:
Sums, unit and currency conversions and times across zones, answered right in
the command palette. Type `12*(3+4)`, `2^10`, `15% * 80`, `sqrt(2)`,
`3h in min`, `72 f to c`, `5 km in mi`, `100 usd in eur`, `$50 to gbp`,
`5pm london in tokyo` or `now in sf`, and the answer comes first in the
results. Return copies it and ⌘Return pastes it. Plain numbers and words get
no answer, so it never crowds a normal search. The panel keeps your last ten
answers.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: network access to `api.frankfurter.dev` for exchange rates. Stackbar 0.21.0 or later.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: turn currency conversion off, and Calculator makes no network requests at all.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel, settings.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Calculate.

facts.label: Units
facts.text: length, mass, time, data, volume and temperature.

facts.label: Currencies
facts.text: the European Central Bank's reference rates (about 30 currencies, updated each working day) from Frankfurter, fetched at launch and every six hours. `$`, `€`, `£`, `¥`, `₹` and names like `euros` work as well as codes.

facts.label: Time zones
facts.text: any city in a time zone's name (`tokyo`, `new york`), plus common ones like `sf`, `nyc`, `bangalore`, `uk` and abbreviations like `pst` and `ist`. Without a starting place, the time is yours.

notes: First version: pick, copy as hex, RGB or HSL, and a list of recent colors.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.color-picke.description:
Pick a color from anywhere on screen and copy it. Run **Pick Color** from the palette (or press the button in the panel), click any pixel with the magnifier, and the color is on your clipboard as hex, RGB or HSL.

**Picked Colors** lists the last 30 colors you picked. Return copies a color in your chosen format, and ⌘1, ⌘2 and ⌘3 copy it as hex, RGB or HSL.

## What it needs

Nothing. The magnifier is macOS's own, and Stackbar 0.26.0 or later.

## Settings

- **Clear Picked Colors** empties the list.

notes: First version: definitions in the palette, copy or open in Dictionary, and recent words.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.dictionary.description:
Look words up in the Mac's own Dictionary without leaving what you're doing. Open the palette, type **Define Word**, then the word, and the definition shows as you type. It works offline.

Return copies the definition, ⌘⇧C copies the word, and ⌘O opens it in the Dictionary app. Words you used stay in a Recent list.

## What it needs

Nothing, and Stackbar 0.26.0 or later. It uses the dictionaries turned on in the Dictionary app's settings, so other languages work too.

notes: Open Shell on a running container opens your terminal app inside it.
CPU and memory for every running container, and the totals at the top of the panel.
Start, restart or stop a whole Compose project from its section, or from the new Docker Compose Projects command.
Stop All Docker Containers, from the palette or a hotkey.
A container's logs open in their own window, so you can keep them beside your editor while the panel closes.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.docker.description:
Your containers in the menu bar. The number is how many are running; the
panel lists them grouped by Compose project, each with its CPU and memory,
Start, Stop, Restart, Open Shell, Logs, Open (for a published port), Copy ID
and Remove,
and each project with Start all, Restart and Stop.

- **Open Shell** (⌘T on a running container) opens your terminal app in
  `docker exec -it <container>`, with bash when the image has it.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `docker`, from Docker Desktop, OrbStack, Colima or Rancher Desktop. No network, files or secrets of its own. Open Shell needs to open your terminal app.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: How it checks
facts.text: `docker ps --all` every 15 seconds while something runs, every minute otherwise, and one `docker stats --no-stream` snapshot while anything runs.

facts.label: Compose
facts.text: a project's buttons run `docker compose -p <project> start|stop|restart`, which finds the project from its containers, so no compose file is needed.

facts.label: When something goes wrong
facts.text: a container that crashes (exits with an error on its own), turns unhealthy or keeps restarting sends a notification, turns the menu bar red with a count, and gets a banner in the panel until it is started again or removed. Stops from the panel don't count.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: show stopped containers, group by Compose project, the trouble notification (on by default), and Remove Stopped Containers (`docker container prune`; images and volumes are left alone).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Docker Containers, Docker Compose Projects, Stop All Docker Containers, Docker Logs (the last 200 lines of one container), Remove Stopped Docker Containers.

facts.label: Requires
facts.text: Stackbar 0.26.0 or later.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `containers` lists every container with its image, state, CPU and memory.

notes: Type a colon and a name, like :tada, in the palette to find an emoji without opening Emoji first.
First release: every emoji in a searchable grid in the palette.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.emoji.description:
An emoji picker in the command palette. Search Emoji opens a grid of every
emoji, grouped as Unicode groups them, with the ones you use most at the top.
Type to narrow it ("party", "thumbs up", "flag japan"), move with the arrow
keys, and press Return to paste the emoji where you were typing. ⌘K copies it
instead. The panel keeps your frequent ones a click from the clipboard.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the clipboard, to paste (your clipboard is put back afterwards). Stackbar 0.20.0 or later, which draws grids in the palette.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Emoji. Give it a hotkey in Settings › Commands.

facts.label: Data
facts.text: Unicode's Emoji 15.1 list and English names, without skin-tone variants. Nothing leaves your Mac.

notes: First release: the palette's file search, now a plugin.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.file-search.description:
Files and folders by name in the command palette, from Spotlight's index.
Type three letters or more and the best matches show under Files in the
results, most recently used first, each with its Finder icon. Return opens
one; ⌘K shows it in Finder or copies its path. Search Files lists up to 20.
Apps, anything inside an app or bundle, hidden files and Library internals
are left out.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: finding files by name with Spotlight (names and paths in your home folder only, nothing is read from inside them), and opening what you pick. Stackbar 0.20.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel (what you opened lately).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Files, which also feeds the palette's results.

notes: The desktop widget has a button: Upgrade All when there are updates, Check when there aren't. Needs Stackbar 0.21.0.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.homebrew.description:
What Homebrew can upgrade, in the menu bar. The number is how many formulae
and casks are outdated; the panel lists them with Upgrade on each row and
Upgrade All at the bottom.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `brew` (Stackbar finds it in `/opt/homebrew/bin` or `/usr/local/bin` and asks you to approve that path once). No network, files or secrets of its own.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: How it checks
facts.text: hourly and on wake it runs `brew outdated --json=v2`, which reads what Homebrew already knows. When that list is more than 6 hours old it runs `brew update` first (from the second check after launch, so the list shows right away), so the count doesn't go stale; the panel says how old the list is. Update Homebrew fetches it now.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: show casks, hide pinned formulae, include casks that update themselves (`--greedy`), fetch the latest formulae every 6 hours (on by default), and a notification when new updates appear.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Upgrade All Homebrew Packages, Update Homebrew, Outdated Homebrew Packages.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `outdated` lists what can be upgraded.

notes: Change an issue's status, comment on it, assign it to yourself or watch it, from its row.
A notification when an issue is assigned to you, louder for Highest and Blocker.
Jira Data Center: pick it in Settings and enter your server and a personal access token.
Updating asks once more for approval, because the plugin can now reach a Data Center server you enter.
Type an issue key like ABC-123 in the palette and the issue comes up first, without opening Jira's command.
A desktop widget shows your open issues.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.jira.description:
Your Jira issues in the menu bar and the palette, on Jira Cloud or Jira Data
Center. The number is how
many assigned issues are in progress; the panel lists them, in progress
first.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: `*.atlassian.net` and the secret `JIRA_API_TOKEN`, an API token from id.atlassian.com (Security > API tokens). Your site and email are set in Settings. On Data Center, `JIRA_SERVER_URL` is your server's address and `JIRA_API_TOKEN` a personal access token; the plugin reaches that server and no other.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: On each issue
facts.text: Open, Change Status (the issue's own workflow), Comment, Assign to Me (on issues that aren't yours yet), Watch, Copy Link, Copy Key, Copy Branch Name (`ABC-123-short-summary`, which Jira's development panel links).

facts.label: Notifications
facts.text: when an issue is newly assigned to you; Highest and Blocker issues say so in the title. Turn it off in Settings.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: My Jira Issues, Search Jira (text, or a key like `ABC-123`), Change Jira Issue Status, Comment on Jira Issue, Create Jira Issue (project, type, summary, description).

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: Cloud or Data Center, site, email, the JQL behind the menu bar and panel (open issues assigned to you by default), notifications, and the default project for new issues.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `assigned` lists your open issues.

notes: First release.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.kill-proces.description:
Find a stuck process by name and end it from the palette. Choose Kill
Process and type part of the name (or a pid): each row shows its CPU and
memory, Return asks it to quit, and ⌘⇧Return force quits it. When several
processes share a name, one action quits them all. The panel lists the
heaviest processes, by CPU or memory.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: running `ps` and `kill`. Stackbar 0.22.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel (the heaviest processes now).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Kill Process.

facts.label: Leaves alone
facts.text: other users' processes, and loginwindow, WindowServer, launchd and Stackbar itself, which would log you out or freeze the screen.

notes: Your Linear inbox in the panel and the palette, with a notification when something new arrives and a bell in the menu bar while it's unread.
Start Work on any issue: In Progress, assigned to you, branch name copied.
Change status, set priority and comment from an issue's row.
Search finds an ID like ENG-123 or a pasted issue link, and says why when it can't search.
Type an issue ID like ENG-42 in the palette and the issue comes up first, without opening Linear's command.
A desktop widget shows your open issues.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.linear.description:
Your Linear issues and inbox in the menu bar and the palette. The number is
how many assigned issues are in progress, or a bell with the unread count
while your inbox has something new; the panel shows new inbox entries, then
groups everything assigned to you by state, ordered by priority.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: `api.linear.app` and the secret `LINEAR_API_KEY`, a personal API key from Linear (Settings > Security & access).

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: On each issue
facts.text: Open, Start Work (moves it to In Progress, assigns it to you and copies the branch name), Change Status, Set Priority, Comment, Copy Branch Name (Linear's own, so the branch links back to the issue), Copy Link, Copy ID.

facts.label: Inbox
facts.text: assignments, mentions and comments, with a notification for each new one. Open marks it read.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: My Linear Issues, Search Linear Issues (by title, or paste an ID like `ENG-123` or an issue link), Linear Inbox, Change Linear Issue Status, Set Linear Issue Priority, Comment on Linear Issue, Create Linear Issue (team, title, description, priority, assign to me).

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: what the menu-bar number counts, inbox notifications, and the default team for new issues.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `assigned` lists your open issues with their branch names.

notes: A LiteLLM Spend command in the palette shows today, 7 and 30 days, and the budget.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.litellm.description:
Tokens, spend and budget from your own [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai)
proxy, with charts. The panel has:

- **Tiles** for today, the last 7 days and the last 30 days, with tokens,
  spend, active days and the daily average.
- **Budget**: spend against your key's budget and when it resets.
- **Activity**: six months of daily tokens as a heatmap.
- **Trend**: a week as bars, or a month or six months as an area chart, in
  tokens or spend.
- **Models**: the top five models over 30 days, with each one's share.
- **Today's requests**: the success rate, how much input came from the
  cache, and what caching saved.

The menu bar shows today's spend, today's tokens or the share of the budget
used (you choose in Settings), and it turns orange at 75% of the budget and
red at 90%.


Ported from vee-plugins' `litellm-cost`.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: two secrets. `LITELLM_PROXY_URL` is your proxy's base URL, like `https://litellm.example.com`, and the plugin can reach that host and no other. `LITELLM_API_KEY` is a LiteLLM key. Both are kept in the Keychain. Nothing is contacted until you enter the URL.

facts.label: Calls
facts.text: `/user/info` and `/user/daily/activity`, every two minutes for the last 30 days and every six hours for the six months before that.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, window, widget, settings.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: what the menu bar shows, and notifications at 90% and 100% of the budget.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `usage_summary`.

notes: First release.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.menu-search.description:
The menus of the app you're in, searchable from the palette, as Raycast's
Search Menu Items has it. In any app, open the palette, choose Search Menu
Items and type part of an item ("export", "view zoom"). Return chooses it.
Each row shows where the item lives (File › Export) and its keyboard
shortcut, so you learn them as you go. The items you choose most rank
higher for that app.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: reading the menus of the app you were in and choosing an item (`.menus`), which uses Accessibility access. Stackbar 0.25.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel (how to use it).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Menu Items.

facts.label: Leaves out
facts.text: the Apple menu, submenu titles and separators. Dimmed items show at the bottom and can't be chosen.

notes: The desktop widget has Play/Pause and Next buttons. Needs Stackbar 0.21.0.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.music.description:
What's playing in Music or Spotify, in the menu bar. Click it to play or
pause; right-click for the panel with the track, Previous, Next and volume.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `osascript`, the only way to talk to Music and Spotify. The install sheet warns that osascript can run any program; this plugin only sends the fixed scripts in its source. macOS asks once whether Stackbar may control Music or Spotify.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: How it checks
facts.text: every 5 seconds, and only players that are already running; it never opens one.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: which player to follow (whichever is playing, Music or Spotify) and what the menu bar shows (title and artist, title, or just the icon).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Play or Pause Music, Next Track, Previous Track, Copy Current Track.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `now_playing` describes the current track.

notes: The end-of-session notification has Start Break (or Start Focus) and 5 More Minutes buttons, unless Auto is on.
A long break every four sessions (or two to six, or off), with dots under the timer for where you are in the round.
The last seven days of focus in a chart under the timer.
Click the timer in the menu bar to start or pause it (turn it off in Settings to open the panel instead).
The desktop widget has a Start/Pause button.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.pomodoro.description:
A focus timer in the Stackbar look: red for focus, teal for breaks. Pick Focus or Break, a preset (25, 50 or
90 minutes of focus; 5, 10 or 15 of break), and press play. The countdown and
the ring around it move on their own, the menu bar shows the time
left (dimmed behind a pause sign while paused), and a chime and a
notification mark the end, with buttons to start the next session or take five more minutes. Today's finished sessions
and focused minutes sit under the timer, with the last seven days in a chart.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: nothing. No network, files or secrets.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: In the panel
facts.text: the tag chip cycles through your tags; skip ends the session without counting it; Auto starts the next session on its own; the note turns the sound on or off; reset clears the timer.

facts.label: Long breaks
facts.text: after four focus sessions (you can pick two to six, or off) the break is a long one, 15 minutes by default. Dots under the timer show how far you are into the round.

facts.label: No lost sessions
facts.text: once a session is a minute in, a mode, preset, skip or reset tap asks first, with a banner to confirm or keep going.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Start or Pause Pomodoro, Start a Focus Session (optional minutes and tag), Take a Break (optional minutes), Skip and Reset. Run them from the palette, give them a hotkey, or call them from a Shortcut or a `stackbar://commands/io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.pomodoro/<command>` link.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: custom focus, break and long-break lengths, how many sessions before a long break, auto-start, the sound, and your tags.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `status` returns the mode, the time left, today's focus and the last seven days.

facts.label: Requires
facts.text: Stackbar 0.26.0 or later.

notes: Type a port number like 3000 or :8080 in the palette to see what is listening on it.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.ports.description:
Which process is listening on which TCP port, and a way to stop it. The
command you'll use most is **Kill Port** from the palette: type `3000` and
whatever holds it is asked to stop.


Processes owned by another user, like system services, can't be stopped
from here.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `lsof` and `kill` (both come with macOS). No network, files or secrets.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel, settings. No menu-bar item.

facts.label: In the panel
facts.text: every listening port with its process and pid, marked local (127.0.0.1 or ::1 only) or open (all interfaces). Each row can open `http://localhost:<port>`, stop the process (SIGTERM), force quit it (SIGKILL) or copy its pid.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: hide ports below 1024 (or 3000).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Kill Port (port, and TERM or KILL), Listening Ports.

facts.label: Agent tool

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.script-comm.description:
Your own scripts as palette commands, in the format Raycast's Script
Commands use, so the scripts you already have work as they are. Put them in
a folder named **Script Commands** in your home folder. Each script with a
`@raycast.title` line becomes a command within a minute (or right away with
Reload Script Commands).

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# @raycast.schemaVersion 1
# @raycast.title Say Hello
# @raycast.mode compact
# @raycast.packageName Demo
# @raycast.argument1 { "type": "text", "placeholder": "Name", "optional": true }
echo "Hello ${1:-world}"
```

facts.label: Modes
facts.text: `silent` shows the last line it prints on screen, `compact` (and `inline`) shows it in the palette, `fullOutput` opens a view with all of it.

facts.label: Also read

facts.label: Interpreters

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the ~/Script Commands folder, running grep (to read the `@raycast.` lines) and those interpreters. Stackbar 0.22.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel (your scripts).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: one for each script, and Reload Script Commands.

notes: First release.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.system-moni.description:
CPU, memory, network and temperature in the menu bar, with the processes
using the most a click away and a notification when something stays high.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `ps`, `sysctl`, `vm_stat`, `netstat`, `df` and `kill` (all come with macOS), and the Mac's temperature sensors and fans, which Stackbar reads for it. No network, files or secrets.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: How it measures
facts.text: every 10 seconds, `ps` gives every process's CPU and memory (total CPU is their sum over the cores), `sysctl` the load, `vm_stat` memory the way Activity Monitor counts it (app memory, wired and compressed, not the file cache), `netstat` the bytes through Wi-Fi and Ethernet, and `df` the disk. Each answers at once, so nothing waits a second between two samples the way `top` does.

facts.label: In the panel
facts.text: a CPU chart for the last five minutes, load averages, memory and disk, download and upload speeds with their recent history, CPU, GPU, SSD and battery temperatures and fan speeds (where the Mac reports them), and the top eight processes, each with Copy PID and Quit Process.

facts.label: Alerts
facts.text: a notification when CPU stays above your line (85% by default) or memory above 90% for a minute, naming the busiest process, and when the disk is 95% full. Once per spell, then quiet for 30 minutes.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: what the menu bar shows (CPU and memory, CPU, memory, or download speed, or CPU temperature), alerts and the CPU line, and whether processes are sorted by CPU or memory.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `usage` returns CPU, memory, disk, network, temperatures and the busiest processes.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.todo.description:
A calm to-do list for the menu bar, in a warm orange. Type a task the way you
would say it and the when comes out of the words: “Call the dentist tomorrow
at 2pm” becomes *Call the dentist*, due tomorrow at 2:00 PM. Today's tasks
(and any left over from earlier) sit on top, then tomorrow, then what is
coming up, then someday. A small ring in the header fills as today's tasks get
done.

Tasks live in **Apple Reminders**, so they're on your iPhone, iPad and Watch
too, and Siri can add to them. Big tasks break into small steps.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: Reminders (`.reminders`). Stackbar asks macOS once. Say no, or pick “This Mac only” in Settings, and tasks stay on this Mac instead.

facts.label: Lists
facts.text: your Reminders lists are Todo's categories. Pick one at the top of the panel to see just that list, type `#groceries` in a task to file it in Groceries, or move a task from its editor. New tasks go to the list on screen, or your default list. (Apple doesn't let apps use Reminders' sections, tags or subtasks, so those stay in the Reminders app.)

facts.label: Steps
facts.text: open a task and choose *Break into steps*, then type a step and press Return for each one. Tap S, M or B to size a step. The task's row shows its next step (small ones first) with a circle to tick it, and how many are done; ticking the last one finishes the task. Type `Plan the offsite: book a venue; send invites` to add a task with its steps in one go. In Reminders, steps are a ☐ checklist at the end of the notes, so you see them on your phone too.

facts.label: Brain dump
facts.text: paste or type several lines and each becomes a task.

facts.label: Sync
facts.text: changes go to Reminders as you make them, and changes from your other devices come in as Reminders gets them. Only the fields you changed are written, so an edit here never undoes one made on your phone. It all works offline; macOS syncs Reminders when you're back online.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: Typing dates
facts.text: today, tonight, tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, friday, this friday, next friday (the Friday of next week), this weekend, next week, next month, in 3 days, in 2 hours, in half an hour, Nov 5, 5 November, the 12th, 2027-03-12. Times: 2pm, 2:30pm, 14:30, at 9, noon, this morning, this afternoon, this evening. Repeats: every day, every weekday, every monday, every week, every month, daily, weekly, monthly. A `!` on its own marks the task important. Words in "double quotes" are kept as they are.

facts.label: In the panel
facts.text: tick the circle to finish a task; tick a done one to bring it back. Click a task to open it in place: rename it (a date in the new text reschedules it), move it to Today, Tomorrow, the weekend, next week or Someday, set a repeat, star it or delete it. Every add, tick, move and delete shows a banner with Undo. The eye button shows what you have done.

facts.label: Repeats
facts.text: ticking off a repeating task records it as done and moves it to its next day.

facts.label: Alerts
facts.text: in Reminders, a task with a time gets a Reminders alert, on every device, with Done and Snooze. On this Mac only, Todo sends one notification when it is due; one the Mac slept through by more than half a day is let go quietly.

facts.label: One nudge
facts.text: optionally, one notification at a time you choose, only on days you haven't ticked anything off, naming a small step to start with.

facts.label: No guilt
facts.text: nothing is ever “overdue” or red. Tasks from earlier days wait under *Still on your list*.

facts.label: Menu bar
facts.text: a quiet count of what is due today, or the next task, the count of everything open, or just the icon. It never turns red.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Add a Todo, Mark a Todo Done, Snooze a Todo (to a time you type, or an hour or a day later) and Today's Todos (a list to tick off from the palette). Run them from the palette, give them a hotkey, or call them from a Shortcut or a `stackbar://commands/io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.todo/add?task=…` link.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: where tasks live, what the menu bar shows, alerts and their sound, the nudge, a morning summary of the day at 7, 8, 9 or 10 AM, and how long done tasks are kept.

facts.label: Agent tools

facts.label: Requires

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.translate.description:
Translates the text you selected. Run **Translate Selection** from the
palette, or give it a hotkey in Settings > Commands. When an app doesn't
share its selection, it uses what you last copied.


  In place, you can paste the result over the selection (your clipboard
  comes back afterwards) or copy it, and the result says which engine did it.
  Text that is already in your target language is translated into your second
  language instead, so one command goes both ways.

facts.label: Engines
facts.text: - **Automatic**, the default, translates in place with no setup. It uses Apple's translation on your Mac when that language pair is downloaded (System Settings > General > Language & Region > Translation Languages), so nothing leaves the Mac. Otherwise it sends the text to Google Translate's keyless endpoint, the one Google's own browser extension uses. Google doesn't document that endpoint, so it may change or be rate limited. - **DeepL:** translates in place with your DeepL API key; the free plan covers 500,000 characters a month. - **Browser:** opens translate.google.com with the text filled in.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the selection (`.context`), the clipboard (as a fallback, and to paste), `translate.googleapis.com`, `api-free.deepl.com` and `api.deepl.com`, and the secret `DEEPL_API_KEY`, which is asked for only when you choose DeepL. Translate Text on Screen reads the screen where you drag (macOS asks for Screen Recording once).

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: the engine, the language to translate into and the second language, and DeepL's formality.

facts.text: calendars to hide, all-day and declined events, only meetings with a link or with other people, the reminder lead time, auto-join, a full-screen alert, how the title shows in the menu bar, and opening calls in their apps.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Join Next Meeting, Copy Next Meeting Link, Today's Meetings, Add Calendar Event ("Lunch with Sam tomorrow 1pm for 45m", "Offsite fri" for all day) and Snooze Meeting Reminder. Give them a hotkey or an alias in Stackbar's Settings, or run them from Spotlight, Shortcuts or a `stackbar://` link.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `next_meeting`, `agenda` and `join_next`.

facts.label: Requires
facts.text: Stackbar 0.26.0 or later.
